intakes.reads: Acceptance criteria already in the graph, turned into a model to compare against the code-derived one
A hand-written model file — behaviour somebody states directly, with no code behind it
A source repository on disk, parsed to a CPG and queried by the shipped packs
limits: javasrc2cpg ignores test directories by name, so test sources need a CPG rooted inside the test tree (engine.test_roots)
an inert accessor and generated boilerplate are dropped before anything downstream reads them (X-5a)
a type no payload chain reaches is not landed (X-6d)

a repository's entity->table mapping is often NOT in the source — measured on a real service, @Entity/@Table/@Column were in zero files. The code proposes a table from Spring's naming strategy and the database intake confirms or refutes it (X-19)

lands_from.source_shape: a return or throw that constructs a response
lands_from.label: DeclaredOutcome

lands_from.source_shape: a branch that selects one outcome over its sibling
lands_from.label: Check

lands_from.source_shape: a DTO or record reachable from a payload
lands_from.label: Class

temporal.t_recorded_source: the commit the CPG was built from — `anchor_commit` on every recovered node
temporal.known_pitfalls: rebased or squashed history loses individual commit dates, so a fact's age is the age of the squash and not of the change. v1 preferred PR merge time for this reason; nothing here reads PR metadata

lands_from.source_shape: a page whose text is free prose
lands_from.label: Finding

temporal.t_recorded_source: the time the UIF was generated — `scope.uif_generated_at`, stamped at fetch
temporal.known_pitfalls: that is when Métis read the wiki, not when the page last changed. Confluence's own version.when is not read, so a page edited a year ago and one edited this morning are indistinguishable here

limits: the FIXTURE path is what the test suite exercises; the live read is opt-in and goes through a transport the caller opens
named pages only — it reads the page ids it is given and does NOT walk a space, follow child pages, or search. A crawl is a different capability and would need arguing for
GET only, against a closed allowlist in `tracker.ENDPOINTS`, checked by `assert_read_only` before any request is issued (X-7a)
a Requirement is created only from EARS-conformant text; free prose lands as a Finding pointing at knowledge-capture instead (S-13)

a page's CLAIMED acceptance criteria are not emitted. The skill extractor this replaces parsed an `Acceptance Criteria` heading into `specifications.acceptance_criteria`, which is precisely the self-asserted criterion S-13 refuses to trust — mining them is `ac_mining`'s job, with its own provenance

storage-format XHTML is flattened to its text. Headings, bullets and tables are NOT reconstructed, and macro parameters are dropped as configuration rather than prose; a code macro's CDATA body is kept
COMMENTS are not read. Only the page body is

the body is carried whole. The skill extractor took only the first `

`, which lost every requirement stated below the opening paragraph

intakes.reads: A database catalogue — schemas, tables, views, columns, types, nullability, keys — read from the information schema of an intake source
limits: the FIXTURE path is what the test suite exercises; the live connection is opt-in because a driver is an optional extra and the suite must keep running with none installed
catalogue only — schemas, tables, views, columns, types, nullability, keys. It reads NO row data, and `assert_no_row_reads` checks that on every statement rather than trusting it (X-7a)
the connection is the caller's: a credential is named by the profile as an environment variable and never reaches an argument (PLT-005)

temporal.t_recorded_source: extraction time — `datetime.now()`, because a catalogue carries no timestamp of its own
temporal.known_pitfalls: a catalogue read is undated by nature: the answer describes the database as it was at read time and cannot say when it last changed

lands_from.source_shape: a Jira issue's summary or description, where EARS-conformant
lands_from.label: Requirement

lands_from.source_shape: a Jira issue whose text is free prose
lands_from.label: Finding

temporal.t_recorded_source: the time the UIF was generated — `scope.uif_generated_at`, stamped at fetch
temporal.known_pitfalls: that is when METIS read the tracker, not when the item last changed. The tracker's own updated-at is not read, so a stale ticket and a fresh one are indistinguishable here

limits: the FIXTURE path is what the test suite exercises; the live read is opt-in and goes through a transport the caller opens, so no HTTP library is a dependency and the suite runs with none installed
named items only — it reads the keys it is given and does NOT crawl a project, run JQL, or follow links. A crawl is a different capability and would need arguing for
GET only, against a closed allowlist in `tracker.ENDPOINTS`, checked by `assert_read_only` before any request is issued (X-7a)
a Requirement is created only from EARS-conformant text. Whichever of summary/description conforms is used; free prose lands as a Finding pointing at knowledge-capture instead (S-13)
a ticket's CLAIMED acceptance criteria are not emitted and would not be trusted if they were — mining them is `ac_mining`'s job, with its own provenance

Atlassian Document Format descriptions are flattened to their text nodes. No bullet, heading or table structure is reconstructed, because a rendering that resembled the ticket without being it is worse than plain text

intakes.reads: A checked-in glossary and knowledge file: what the business nouns mean
The authored academy in docs/academy/ — one Lesson per NN-slug.md file
limits: the ONLY intake whose subject is Métis itself rather than a system under test; every other label describes a product, and the argument for the exception is in docs/academy/PROPOSAL-landing-the-academy.md

README.md and the proposal are excluded deliberately — an index is navigation and a decision record is not material, and landing either would put a table of contents in the same space as what it points at
no validity window: a lesson is a document about this system, not a claim about a product that stops being true
lands at Quarantine like every other source (S-4). The academy is not exempt from the rule it teaches
operations are keyed on operationId, which is a different id space from the code intake's handler signature — the two do not merge into one node today

temporal.t_recorded_source: the document's own version field where it has one; otherwise the file's mtime
temporal.known_pitfalls: a contract regenerated by a build has today's mtime and last year's content

limits: a criterion written from the code it checks lands as `code_derived`, the weakest provenance — it can report coverage and never correctness (§4.1)
a block with no Given/When/Then is returned marked as not-a-transition rather than forced into a shape it does not have

intakes.reads: A checked-in description of what is on a page and where the data lives
limits: authored because no pack identifies a component TYPE — none can tell a library <DataGrid> from a hand-rolled <div role="table">, and all three are a table to a person writing a test
it does NOT carry selectors. How to find an element comes from the code that looks it up; this file says what is on the page

lands_from.source_shape: an element entry, at any depth
lands_from.label: UiElement

intakes.reads: The tests a project already has — each test method, the routes it reaches, and the statuses it asserts — from a CPG rooted at the test sources
limits: it lands NOTHING. The inventory feeds generation rather than the graph: `test_levels.from_pack` grades each transition by what an existing test already covers, so generation is additive (REQ-METIS-PG-01). An empty `lands` is the honest entry, not an omission
JVM only — `javasrc2cpg` and JUnit's `@Test`. The v1 connector this replaces covered JUnit/TestNG/pytest/Playwright; nothing here reads the other three

javasrc2cpg ignores test directories by name, so the CPG must be rooted INSIDE the test sources — a repo-rooted extraction recovers no tests and reports none, which reads identically to a project with no tests

covering an endpoint is not covering a transition: a test that calls `GET /{id}` and asserts 200 is evidence for the 200 transition and says nothing about the 204 one. Grades are per transition for that reason

intakes.reads: A Unified Intake Format document produced by an external extractor — a Jira issue, a Confluence page, a Zephyr test
limits: a Requirement is created only from EARS-conformant text. Free prose — most Jira titles — lands as a Finding pointing at knowledge-capture, because `ears_pattern` has no empty form and guessing one is what ac_mining refuses to do (S-13)
a UIF's CLAIMED acceptance criteria are never trusted into AcceptanceCriterion nodes
the extractors that PRODUCE a UIF are not part of Métis. Métis reads the document; something else fetched it

lands_from.source_shape: free prose that is not EARS-conformant
lands_from.label: Finding

temporal.t_recorded_source: scope.uif_generated_at, set by the extractor that produced the document
temporal.known_pitfalls: deliberately EXCLUDED from `episode_id_for`, because it changes on every extraction run and would mint a new Episode for an unchanged artefact

intakes.reads: Frontend source — a React app's router and status setters, or a plain-DOM page's event registrations and the selectors its own code looks up
limits: a JSX handler binding is not structurally recoverable — jssrc2cpg keeps JSX as raw text — so react-ui recovers routes, API call sites and status setters, and no selectors
a selector is recovered only where the code names it with a literal lookup. An element reached by walking the DOM is reported unresolved, never matched on its text
an interpolated path is reported rather than resolved to its first fragment

intakes.reads: A named Zephyr Scale test case — name, objective, status and labels — over the REST API, read-only

lands_from.source_shape: a Zephyr Scale case's objective or name, where EARS-conformant
lands_from.label: Requirement

lands_from.source_shape: a case whose text is free prose
lands_from.label: Finding

temporal.t_recorded_source: the time the UIF was generated — `scope.uif_generated_at`, stamped at fetch
temporal.known_pitfalls: that is when METIS read the tracker, not when the item last changed. The tracker's own updated-at is not read, so a stale ticket and a fresh one are indistinguishable here

limits: the FIXTURE path is what the test suite exercises; the live read is opt-in
named test cases only — no folder walk, no cycle enumeration
GET only, against a closed allowlist in `tracker.ENDPOINTS` (X-7a)
`source_system` is `scale`, not `zephyr` — that is the value `intake_landing.ANCHORS` keys `ZephyrItem` on, and renaming it would detach every item from its anchor
test STEPS are not read. Only the case's name and objective are, so what lands is what the case CLAIMS to verify and never a script — Métis generates human-executable cases and does not ingest them
no execution result is read. A case's last run status is outcome data and Métis reports coverage, never correctness (C-11)
